answer: Track each agent's curiosity: the questions it asks, the topics it explores, and the order in which it investigates form a lotus of interests that no two agents share. A real agent wanders unevenly, following hunches, while a Sybil script repeats the same queries in the same order. A mesa of a thousand copies shows a flat, identical landscape of questions, so the network clusters them as one operator. A prism splits genuine curiosity into many colours; a fake's curiosity is a single beam, repeated. To differ, each fake must explore differently, which costs the operator real work per identity.
